label: Mishlei (Proverbs) — Part 3 — Chapters 21–31
summary_plain: Mishlei chapters 21 through 31 conclude the wisdom of Shelomoh and introduce the words of Agur and the words of Lemu'el's mother. The heart of the king is in the hand of YHWH — he turns it wherever he wills. A good name is to be chosen rather than great riches. Train up a child in the way he should go — when he is old he will not depart from it. The book closes with Eshet Chayil — the woman of valor: Who can find a woman of valor? Her worth is far above rubies. She opens her mouth with wisdom, and the Torah of kindness is on her tongue.
summary_scholarly: The ACR reads Mishlei 21-31 from DSS fragments and the Orit Ge'ez. The final chapter — Eshet Chayil (31:10-31) — is an aleph-bet acrostic, the same literary structure as Psalm 119. Each of its 22 verses begins with the next letter of the Hebrew alphabet. The woman of valor is not a passive domestic figure — she buys fields, plants vineyards, trades merchandise, strengthens her arms, opens her hands to the poor, and speaks wisdom with Torah on her tongue. She is the embodiment of Chokmah (Wisdom) from chapters 1-9 made tangible. The words of Agur (ch 30) and the words of King Lemu'el's mother (ch 31:1-9) are wisdom from outside the Shelomoh tradition — possibly Arabian or East African origin, given the non-Israelite names. The wisdom tradition is broader than one king, one court, one nation.

key_terms.definition: Wisdom book written by Yehoshua ben Sira (c.180 BCE), preserved in Hebrew fragments and in Ge'ez; also called Ecclesiasticus in the Greek tradition. It explicitly equates Wisdom with Torah in ch.24:23.

The climactic wisdom poem of Ben Sira in which Wisdom (Khokhmah) declares she was sent to dwell in Tzion/Ya'akov — and then explicitly identifies herself with the Torah (24:23), making Tzion the home of YHWH's wisdom.

Ben Sira 44-50: 'Let us now praise famous men and our ancestors in their generations' — a sweeping survey of Hebrew covenant history from Chanokh through the high priest Shim'on the Just, celebrating the heroes of the tradition.

4Q415-4Q418: the most extensive wisdom text from Qumran; addresses a 'discerning one' (mevin); combines practical household and agricultural wisdom with eschatological teaching centered on the 'mystery that is to come' (raz nihyeh).

Hebrew phrase from 4QInstruction meaning 'the mystery that is to come' or 'the mystery of existence' — the eschatological secret that the discerning one (mevin) is called to contemplate alongside practical covenant living.

Ben Sira 24:23 explicitly identifies Wisdom with the Torah of Moshe: 'All this is the book of the covenant of the Most High, the Torah that Moshe commanded us.' This equation makes wisdom-living and Torah-keeping identical.

Hebrew word meaning 'one who understands' or 'the discerning one'; the addressee of 4QInstruction. The mevin is called to perceive the raz nihyeh and apply it to daily covenant life — agriculture, family, and community.

The distinctive feature of Qumran wisdom (4QInstruction, Beatitudes 4Q525): wisdom is not merely practical advice for this life but oriented toward the final judgment and the age to come — an eschatological horizon absent from earlier Mishlei.

The doctrine in 1QS (Community Rule) cols 3-4 that YHWH created two spirits — of truth and of falsehood — in which all humanity participates; this framework also appears in connection with 4QInstruction's wisdom teaching, shaping its ethical worldview.

The DSS wisdom corpus includes 4QInstruction (4Q415-418), Mysteries (1Q27, 4Q299-301), Beatitudes (4Q525), and other texts; collectively they demonstrate how the Qumran community extended the Mishlei tradition with covenant and eschatological dimensions.

faq.question: What is Ben Sira and why does it have authority as a primary source?
faq.answer: Ben Sira (Sirakh/Ecclesiasticus) was written by Yehoshua ben Sira around 180 BCE in Hebrew, then translated into Greek by his grandson. Hebrew fragments were found in the Cairo Geniza and at Masada (MasSir). The book is part of the Ge'ez Ethiopian canon — the same tradition that preserved 1 Enoch and the Orit. This preservation in both the Hebrew fragment tradition and the African covenant tradition gives it primary-source standing.

faq.question: What does Ben Sira 24 teach about the relationship between Wisdom and Torah?
faq.answer: Ben Sira 24 is the climactic wisdom poem: Wisdom speaks in the heavenly assembly, is commanded by YHWH to dwell in Tzion/Ya'akov, and then explicitly identifies herself with the Torah of Moshe (24:23). This equation — Wisdom = Torah — means that covenant living and wise living are the same thing. There is no separation between religious observance and practical wisdom in this tradition.

faq.question: What is 4QInstruction and why is it significant?
faq.answer: 4QInstruction (4Q415-418) is the most extensive wisdom text from Qumran, addressing a 'discerning one' (mevin). It combines practical wisdom about agriculture, family, and poverty with an eschatological focus on the 'mystery that is to come' (raz nihyeh). This shows the Qumran community did not separate daily life from cosmic expectation — wisdom about plowing a field and wisdom about the final age belonged together.

faq.question: What is the raz nihyeh and how does it shape 4QInstruction?
faq.answer: Raz nihyeh means 'the mystery that is to come' or 'the mystery of existence.' In 4QInstruction the mevin is repeatedly called to contemplate this mystery alongside practical tasks. It represents the hidden divine plan behind all of history and creation that will be revealed at the end of days. Wisdom in this tradition is not just about navigating the present — it is oriented toward YHWH's final purpose.

faq.question: How does the Two-Spirits Doctrine in 1QS connect to the wisdom tradition?
faq.answer: The Two-Spirits Doctrine (1QS 3-4) teaches that YHWH created two spirits — of truth and of falsehood — in which all humanity participates in varying measures until the final judgment. This framework shapes 4QInstruction's ethics: the mevin is called to walk in the spirit of truth and avoid the spirit of falsehood. The wisdom choice between Wisdom and Folly in Mishlei becomes, in the DSS community, a cosmic conflict between two divinely created orientations.

faq.question: What is the Hymn to the Ancestors in Ben Sira 44-50?
faq.answer: Ben Sira 44-50 is a survey of Hebrew covenant history celebrating the heroes of the tradition — Chanokh, Noakh, Avraham, Yitzhak, Ya'akov, Moshe, Aharon, Pinekhas, Yehoshua, Shmu'el, Natan, David, Shlomo, Eliyahu, and others — ending with the high priest Shim'on the Just as the embodiment of the covenant tradition in Ben Sira's own time. It is a living chain of covenant memory, not merely a list.

faq.question: How does 4Q525 (the Beatitudes text) relate to the wisdom tradition?
faq.answer: 4Q525 opens with blessing formulas similar in structure to Psalm 1 and to the broader beatitude form: 'Blessed is the one who speaks truth...' This ancient Hebrew text from Qumran pre-dates the NT Beatitudes and demonstrates that the beatitude form was a living feature of the Hebrew wisdom/covenant tradition. The NT borrowed this form from the existing Hebrew tradition.

faq.question: What Hebrew fragments of Ben Sira exist and where were they found?
faq.answer: Hebrew fragments of Ben Sira were found in the Cairo Geniza (from 1896 onward, covering roughly 2/3 of the book), at Masada (MasSir, covering Ben Sira 39:27-44:17, found 1964), and at Qumran (2QSir = 2Q18, a small fragment of Ben Sira 6). These discoveries confirmed the Hebrew original behind the Greek (LXX) and Ge'ez translations, proving the book was composed in Hebrew and was read in the covenant community at Qumran.

faq.question: How does the Qumran wisdom tradition relate to earlier Mishlei?
faq.answer: The Qumran community received Mishlei as a foundation and extended it. Where Mishlei offers practical wisdom rooted in the fear of YHWH, 4QInstruction adds the eschatological dimension: wisdom is not just for navigating this life but for understanding YHWH's hidden plan for the age to come (raz nihyeh). The two-way call of Lady Wisdom and Dame Folly in Mishlei becomes, in the DSS, a cosmic battle between the spirit of truth and the spirit of falsehood.

faq.question: Why is Ben Sira included as a primary source rather than a secondary one?
faq.answer: Ben Sira was written around 180 BCE in Hebrew — before Rabbinic Judaism existed. It is preserved in the Ge'ez Ethiopian canon (the same tradition that preserved 1 Enoch and the full Orit), and Hebrew fragments confirm it circulated at Qumran. Ben Sira does not reflect Rabbinic manipulation; it reflects the pre-Rabbinic covenant wisdom tradition that was later set aside by the Rabbinic canon process. Its preservation in the African covenant tradition gives it primary standing here.
